capacity_checks.notes: 112 grid; c^2<a^2+b^2 ->102; c!=b ->90 (the '90 raw'); gcd(a,b,|c|)=1 ->78. All 12 removed tuples reduce to admitted primitives. All 78 have exactly two distinct roots in (0,360) (independent sympy half-angle oracle agrees; max residual 5.8e-15); closest root to an endpoint 12.97 deg; min root separation 36.87 deg; c=b is exactly the endpoint-root case. Decision classes: c>b (anchor-like Q1/Q2) 7; 0<c<b (needs 180-p and 360+p) 22; c=0 11; c<0 38. 26 tuples have an integer root (90/180/270 or 135/315). Part (a) has only 16 distinct prompts / 11 distinct alpha values, each (a,b) reused 2-7 times.
24 distinct exact x; one identical decision (take sine, divide); variation = 3 exact values x sign x divisor k.

24 parameter tuples but k never affects the response: 6 distinct targets (3 up to sign), one identical decision and conclusion ('no real solution') for every instance; 8 of 24 share the same forward-sine trap value 0. Semantic decision capacity is 6 at most.

findings.expected: Answer-only rule agrees with the question wording and with NSSCAS conventions; any instruction the learner is given ('showing the principal-value step') is tied to a criterion.
findings.actual: Every admissible question says 'exactly, using radians and showing the principal-value step', yet no criterion credits the principal-value step (V-M1 is kx=sin(theta), V-A1 is x) and a bare correct x earns 2/2 by 'implied transformation'. The work order asks the reviewer to confirm this rule.
findings.evidence: Cambridge anchor wording (9709_m16_qp_12 p2) has no 'show'; its scheme (ms p4) carries no implied/soi note. NSSCAS 2021 report PDF236: 'Complete methods should be shown at all times' and 'No marks are awarded if only answers are given'. recipe-contract.md: a final value may leave a method requirement unevidenced. So a learner following the instruction gains nothing and one ignoring it gets full marks.
findings.repair: Not confirmed. Choose one: (i) use the anchor wording ('Solve ..., giving the solution in an exact form'), drop the unmarked 'principal-value step' and the vacuous 'using radians', and set answer-only explicitly (NSSCAS-consistent: 0, or at most A1); or (ii) keep the instruction and add a credited criterion (e.g. B1 'theta in [-pi/2,pi/2] stated' -> 3 marks) with answer-only capped below full marks.

findings.expected: The recipe's stated independent target ('respect the principal output range before taking sine') is a live learner decision in at least one branch.
findings.actual: admissible-linear: the range check earns nothing and the routine 'take sine, divide by k' gives full marks whether or not the learner knows the range (same as the Cambridge item). range-obstruction: the answer is always 'no real solution', the question names the method ('using the principal range') and a bare 'no real solution' earns 1/2, so the outcome is guessable. No instance ever requires the learner to decide between solving and rejecting.
findings.evidence: Exemplars lines 9-51; WO table line 25 rationale 'after respecting the principal range' is not reflected in V-M1/V-A1; obstruction memo line 50. PLAN.md:40 claims 'Correct principal-range reasoning, including an impossible target'.
findings.repair: Make the decision live: e.g. one branch 'Solve sin^-1(kx)=theta, or explain why there is no real solution' drawing theta from both admissible and out-of-range sets (credit B1 range comparison, then M1/A1 or B1 conclusion), or neutral wording in both branches so the outcome is not given away. At minimum reword the PLAN/WO claim so the admissible branch is described as exact special-angle recovery only.

findings.expected: Capacity counts distinct learner decisions/responses (recipe-contract: swapped names/another seed are not capacity).
findings.actual: Capacity 24 multiplies 6 targets by k in {2..5}, but k never enters the correct response or the explanation; all 24 have the identical conclusion. 8 tuples share the same trap value x=0.
findings.evidence: Enumerated with sympy: 24 tuples, 6 distinct targets, 17 distinct forward-sine trap values, one conclusion.
findings.repair: Report semantic capacity 6 (3 up to sign) for range-obstruction and key no-repeat on theta, or redesign per trig-02 so k matters. Total '48' should not be presented as 48 distinct decisions.

findings.expected: Each criterion awarded only for what its definition requires; valid alternative arguments credited.
findings.actual: X-B2 is defined as 'concludes no real solution because the supplied target is outside it', but a bare 'no real solution' (no reason) is awarded X-B2 (1/2) in an 'Explain' question whose answer is always 'no'. The valid contradiction route (kx=sin(theta) gives x, but sin^-1(kx) then equals the principal value pi/3 != 2pi/3) is not addressed; the memo would give it 0 unless the interval is stated separately.
findings.evidence: WO line 44 vs line 50; exemplar line 37-39 itself uses this substitution as a check.
findings.repair: Award 0 for an unexplained conclusion (or redefine X-B2 as conclusion-only and say so); credit the substitution-contradiction argument (it uses the principal value) at least X-B2, X-B1 if the principal value/range is stated.

findings.expected: Adapted M1 no stricter than the anchor without a stated reason.
findings.actual: V-M1 requires the 'exact forward ratio'; the Cambridge anchor scheme accepts the decimal (-0.866) at the M1 stage and reserves exactness for A1.
findings.repair: Allow a correct decimal forward ratio (e.g. 5x=0.707) for V-M1; keep V-A1 exact. Also state the decimal rule per answer: only 1/(2k) values are rational and of those 1/6 (k=3) is non-terminating.

findings.expected: Credit for part (b) agrees with its 'Hence solve' wording and NSSCAS hence/answer-only conventions; recipe-contract: alternative methods earn credit 'unless the question explicitly restricts the method'.
findings.actual: A naked pair of roots earns b-A1+b-A2 (2/4); a route bypassing the hence reduction still earns both accuracy marks; 'fully correct roots by a direct sinusoid method still earn 4/4'.
findings.evidence: 2021 report PDF236: 'If the question states hence and the previous question is not used, no marks may be awarded for the solution'; 'No marks are awarded if only answers are given'. Official caps when hence not used: 2023 P2 Q6(b) 'SC1: Correct but hence not used' (PDF337); 2022 P1 Q2(b) 'SC1 if relationship is not seen' (PDF301). The 2022 Q6 note 'A1 can be awarded without M2' (PDF313) refers to the dependent second M, not to answer-only or non-hence work.
findings.repair: Either keep 'Hence' and set: answer-only 0 (or SC1 for both correct roots), non-hence complete method SC1 maximum; or change the wording to 'Hence, or otherwise,' and then credit alternative complete methods fully. Update the 5/7 answer-only statement in WO:55 accordingly.

findings.expected: Memo describes the root-selection decision correctly for every admitted class.
findings.actual: WO:53 'For negative c or zero, the correct corresponding sine branches replace the anchor's positive first/second-quadrant restriction' implies positive c keeps the anchor's p and 180-p pattern. That holds only when c>b (7/78). For 0<c<b (22/78, including the normal exemplar (3,4,2)) the calculator value p gives theta=p-alpha<0 and the second root needs 360+p. A marker following WO:53 could award b-M2 for 'theta+alpha=23.58 and 156.42' in the normal case. WO:34 likewise describes only a positive/negative split.
findings.evidence: Enumeration: c>b 7, 0<c<b 22, c=0 11, c<0 38. Normal case: p=23.578 < alpha=53.130, transformed roots 156.42 and 383.58 (exemplar line 31). Anchor 2022 Q6 is c>b (2.4>sqrt5).
findings.repair: Replace the sentence with the three decision classes and the b-M2 evidence for each (p,180-p when p>alpha; 180-p,360+p when 0<p<alpha; 180-p,360+p for p<0; 180,360 for c=0). Add the commonest wrap error to the response examples (e.g. -29.6 with 103.3) with its marks and feedback.

findings.expected: Extra-answer cap is unambiguous and matches the source treatment of out-of-domain values.
findings.actual: 'If more than two inequivalent roots are submitted, b-A2 is not awarded ... Equivalent duplicate notation for one root does not count as a third root.' A learner giving 103.3, 330.4 and -29.6 offers -29.6, which is coterminal with 330.4 and is a genuine root of the equation outside the interval; the rule can be read either way.
findings.evidence: 2022 report PDF312 (Q6(b)(i)): candidates who used the general solution and gave solutions outside the given domain lost an accuracy mark; award table PDF313 'A0 if more than 2 answers'.
findings.repair: Define the cap on submitted final values: any value outside 0<theta<360, including coterminal angles, counts as an extra answer; only re-statements of the same value count as duplicates.

findings.expected: Admitted tuples are not rounding knife-edges, or the memo states how answers from reasonable intermediate rounding are treated.
findings.actual: Using 2-dp alpha with a full-precision principal angle never changes a 1-dp root (78/78 checked). Rounding the principal angle to 2 dp as well changes a root in 6 tuples: (2,4,+-1), (3,4,+-2), (4,1,+-3), including the normal exemplar (3,4,2): 360+23.58-53.13=330.45 -> 330.5, while the memo answer is 330.4 (exact 330.448076). (1,4,+-3) and (4,1,+-3) have roots within 0.0001 deg of a rounding boundary (57.35010, 237.35010, 32.64990, 212.64990): even 3-dp alpha with exact p changes the 1-dp answer.
findings.evidence: Script output in trigwork/rform_round2.py. NSSCAS award PDF313 itself writes theta+48.19 deg (2-dp alpha carried); 2021 report PDF236 and 2023 PDF337 say premature rounding loses accuracy marks, so 330.5 would get A0 c.a.o.
findings.repair: Exclude (1,4,+-3) and (4,1,+-3) (capacity 74), and either exclude the other knife-edge tuples or state explicitly that answers from premature rounding get A0 with 'premature rounding' feedback rather than a method diagnosis. Pick a normal exemplar that is not a knife-edge, or show the 330.45 trap in its solution.

findings.expected: Capacity and no-repeat exposure reported per assessed part (recipe-contract: exposure keys identify shared assessed subparts).
findings.actual: Capacity 78 is keyed on (a,b,c), but part a-convert depends only on (a,b): 16 distinct prompts with 11 distinct alpha values (proportional pairs (1,1)/(2,2)/(3,3)/(4,4), (1,2)/(2,4), (2,1)/(4,2) share alpha), each repeated 2-7 times across the 78. A learner can be served the same 3-mark conversion up to 7 times as 'fresh'.
findings.repair: Report a-convert capacity 16 (11 phase decisions) separately from b-roots 78, and key a-convert exposure by (a,b) so repeated conversions are disclosed or treated as after-feedback evidence.
